note: HAND-AUTHORED. This is the ONLY file in data/ that is not generated by tools/build_data.mjs - do not let the builder overwrite it. Keys under `vs` are character keys from characters.json (internal ids: K22 = The Twins). Keys under `perks` are perk keys from perks.json and are all role=survivor. Counterplay is deliberately mechanical and evergreen (loops, line of sight, pallet economy, what the power physically does) rather than patch-number tier claims, so it does not rot between patches. Entries flagged `fromPowerText` were written from the power description in characters.json/powers.json rather than from play knowledge.

Chuckles.threat: Bear Traps turn strong loops, window landings and hook areas into an 8-second down that he does not have to be present for.
counters: Enter tiles from open ground - he pre-traps the pallet mouth, the window landing and the grass at the entrance.
Disarm every trap you walk past instead of stepping around it; a disarmed trap is one he has to walk back and reset.
Free a trapped teammate immediately - the escape attempt can take a very long time and he is already walking over.
Tall grass is the danger zone: crouch through it or path around it rather than sprinting a blind line.
Once you know a tile is clean, keep coming back to it - a trap-free loop is a genuinely safe loop against a 4.6 m/s M1 killer.
avoid: Sprinting the same grassy shortcut twice - he re-traps it after the first chase.
Dropping a pallet and immediately vaulting the window he already trapped.

Bob.threat: Cloaked he is near-invisible, Undetectable and faster than you; the uncloak is the only warning you get before a hit.
counters: Learn the bell and the shimmer - the uncloak has a fixed animation, so start running the moment you hear it.
He cannot attack while cloaked, so every approach is telegraphed - hold your pallet a beat longer than you would against an M1 killer.
Repair with your back to open ground so a cloaked approach has to cross your field of view.
Flashlights and firecrackers burn him out of cloak; a beam on an uncloaking Wraith buys the entire tile.
avoid: Panic-dropping the pallet the instant you hear the bell - he can body-block the tile and re-cloak.
Reading silence as safety; a cloaked Wraith has no terror radius at all.

HillBilly.threat: An instant-down chainsaw sprint on a killer who also traverses the map faster than anyone - there is no safe far-away gen.
counters: Break line of sight early. The chainsaw needs a straight run-up, so a curved path or a jungle gym forces a bump.
At loops hug the wall tight - his curve is limited and a bumped wall is a long stun.
Drop pallets slightly earlier than usual; being caught in the open is a one-hit down, not a health state.
He commits to a line once he revs, so a hard 90-degree turn into an obstacle is the standard dodge.
avoid: Running the long open lanes between buildings.
Vaulting a window and then running straight away from it - that is the exact shape his sprint wants.

Nurse.threat: Blinks ignore every pallet, wall and window in the game, so the whole loop layer of survivor play simply does not apply.
counters: Break line of sight, then move unpredictably - she aims at where she believes you are, so a hold-still or a double-back beats any straight run.
Stay against tall solid walls and force her to blink blind.
Her post-blink fatigue is your only free distance; spend it reaching a completely different tile, never on re-looping the same one.
She is 3.85 m/s and slow between chases - splitting up and holding gens is the real counter, not out-looping her.
avoid: Running predictable pallet loops - she blinks straight over them.
Sprinting a long straight line; it is the easiest blink in the game to land.

Witch.threat: Phantasm traps make every place she has already been permanently dangerous - hooks, gens and pallets all become teleport tripwires.
counters: Crouch through trap zones. Crouching does not trigger her traps at all.
Burn traps out with a flashlight beam to delete them outright.
She is 4.4 m/s and hates leaving her web - pressure the far side of the map away from her trap cluster.
Never sprint straight into a hook rescue; the ground around a hook is the first place she traps.
avoid: Rushing a rescue and setting off three traps in a row.
Skipping traps you could have crouched past because you were in a hurry.

Shape.threat: Tier 1 is almost invisible with a tiny terror radius; Tier 3 is a timed instant-down window where every tile is on a clock.
counters: Deny stalk: break line of sight whenever he is looking at you, and work gens from behind cover rather than in the open.
In Tier 3 do not hold pallets - drop early and stretch distance until it expires.
Tier 1 Myers is offensively harmless; bank gen progress in that window instead of hiding from it.
Watch your teammates' exposure too - a Myers denied stalk by you will just farm whoever never breaks line of sight.
avoid: Staring at him across the map - every second of line of sight is free stalk.
Holding a pallet in Tier 3 hoping for a stun.

Killer07.threat: Static Blast reveals everyone in his terror radius on demand and Madness forces screams and illusionary doubles - he never truly loses you.
counters: Accept that you will be found and play for strong tiles instead of stealth; hiding just costs gen time.
Snap out of Madness while he is chasing someone else, never with him walking at you.
His shock has a wind-up and a limited cone - vault or drop the pallet before it lands, or step out of the cone.
Illusionary Doctors do not move like him and bring no terror radius change; do not abandon a gen for one.
avoid: Trying to stealth a Doctor.
Snapping out of Madness mid-chase and eating the free hit.

Bear.threat: Ranged instant pressure at any distance, plus a lullaby that tells you she is coming without telling you from where.
counters: Keep geometry between you and her - a hatchet stopped by a rock is a free reload or wind-up for you.
Serpentine only in the open; at loops hug the wall so the hatchet clips it.
She is 4.4 m/s while not winding up, so a real tile is a genuinely winning loop if you deny the throw.
Force reloads - once her hatchets are gone she has to walk to a locker.
avoid: Running long open lanes.
Vaulting a window in her line of sight - the vault animation is the free hatchet.

Cannibal.threat: A chainsaw sweep that instant-downs and can catch multiple survivors at once, which makes hooks and the basement genuinely lethal.
counters: Force the tantrum: hold the pallet, make him sweep into it, and he loses his whole charge bank.
Stay tight at loops - the sweep does not turn well and a bumped wall ends it.
Never crowd a hook while he is close; a camping Bubba wins the moment three people stand in one doorway.
Stagger your rescues so one sweep cannot catch two people.
avoid: Bunching up at a hook or on the basement stairs.
Running a straight line while he is revving - that is the exact shape of the sweep.

Nightmare.threat: Asleep you are slowed by snares or blocked by fake pallets, he can teleport to any generator, and you cannot see him until he is close.
counters: Wake up on purpose - fail a skill check, use an alarm clock, or have an awake teammate wake you.
Dream pallets are fake. A pallet in a spot that never had one is a trap, so keep running.
His teleport telegraphs on the gen you are repairing - leave and rotate instead of eating the free hit.
Keep at least one survivor awake; awake players are the safe rescuers.
avoid: Staying asleep all match because waking up is inconvenient.
Trusting a pallet that appeared in a tile with no pallet spawn.

Pig.threat: Reverse Bear Traps convert generator progress into a death timer, and her ambush dash punishes anyone looping predictably.
counters: Search boxes early. Traps only tick once a generator is completed, so get it off before the last gens go.
Never finish the last generator while a teammate still has a live trap on their head.
The ambush has a loud growl and a fixed charge - drop the pallet or vault the moment you hear it start.
Uncrouching costs her time, so a stealthed Pig near your gen has already committed.
avoid: Popping the last generator with a trapped teammate still searching boxes.
Holding a loop against a fully charged ambush.

Clown.threat: The tonic strips your ability to win a loop by slowing you and blurring the screen, and the antidote makes him faster right afterwards.
counters: Play the tile BEFORE the gas lands. Once you are gassed at a loop, that loop is already lost.
Force reloads - he carries a limited number of bottles.
Run through his yellow antidote cloud yourself; it speeds survivors up too.
Pre-drop and keep moving to the next tile instead of trying to out-loop the slow.
avoid: Committing to a long loop while already slowed.
Standing in a purple cloud arguing with a pallet.

Spirit.threat: While phasing she is invisible and directionless to you; the entire matchup runs on the sound and scratch marks you give her.
counters: Stop producing information - walk instead of running and break the scratch-mark line before she commits.
When she phases, do the unexpected: hold still, walk sideways, or double back on your own path.
Grass moves as she passes and her cosmetics make noise - play the audio, not the sightline.
Her phase has a real cooldown; bank gen progress while she is recharging.
avoid: Sprinting a straight predictable line the moment she phases.
Loudly vaulting right before a phase - you just told her exactly where you are.

Legion.threat: Feral Frenzy chains hits across the whole team and puts everyone into Deep Wound, buying enormous map-wide time for nothing.
counters: Break line of sight during a frenzy chain - he has to see the next target to keep it going.
Spread out. A stacked team is a free four-hit chain.
Mend somewhere he is not about to rotate back through, not on the gen he just left.
Once the frenzy ends he is a plain M1 killer with a stun - that is when you actually loop him.
avoid: Running toward your teammates while he is in frenzy.
Mending in the open in the middle of his patrol route.

Plague.threat: Cleansing at a fountain hands her a ranged instant-injure Corrupt Purge, so the match is a trap: stay sick, or arm her.
counters: Stay broken on purpose. Cleansing is usually the wrong play unless she is already corrupt.
If someone has to cleanse, do it while she is far away and already holding Corrupt Purge.
You will be injured all match, so build for injured value instead of fighting it.
Break line of sight to deny the vomit stream - it needs a clear cone to land.
avoid: Cleansing early because you want to feel healthy.
Bunching up while sick - it spreads through pools and contact.

Ghostface.threat: Undetectable on demand plus a personal stalk that exposes you outright - three unseen seconds of staring is a one-shot down.
counters: Reveal him. Look at him long enough and the shroud breaks and he is locked out of it for a while.
Check gen sightlines constantly; his stalk needs sustained line of sight to build.
Once exposed, play it like Myers Tier 3 - pre-drop and stretch distance until it decays.
Crouched Ghostface is slow, so every stealth approach is time you should be spending on gens.
avoid: Tunnel-visioning a generator with your back to open ground.
Running away instead of turning and revealing him.

Demogorgon.threat: Portals give near-instant map traversal and Shred is a lunging instant-hit that beats most window and pallet timings.
counters: Seal portals whenever you find them - it costs him his entire travel game.
Shred is long and committed; a late pallet drop or a tight wall hug makes him whiff it.
He roars loudly when he leaves a portal - treat it as a warning to rotate off that gen.
At jungle gyms, hold the tile: a Shred through a window costs him the follow-up.
avoid: Leaving portals up for the whole match.
Panic-vaulting into an already-charged Shred.

Oni.threat: Blood orbs dropped by injured survivors charge Blood Fury, which is a fast instant-down demon dash that ignores your normal loop timings.
counters: Do not stay injured. Injured survivors literally leave the fuel for his power on the ground.
During Blood Fury, pre-drop everything and chain tiles - do not try to time a pallet against the dash.
Spread out so his orb collection route is long and unrewarding.
Blood Fury is on a timer. A good pallet chain outlasts it and he ends up with nothing.
avoid: Leaving a trail of blood orbs while you finish a gen.
Holding a pallet for the stun mid-Blood Fury.

Gunslinger.threat: A ranged harpoon that ignores pallets and windows and reels you into an M1 hit - no loop against him is completely safe.
counters: Break line of sight. The spear needs a clear shot and his aim-down has a long wind-up.
Play short, tight, high-walled loops; he cannot shoot through geometry.
If speared, run perpendicular to the chain so it snaps on an obstacle.
He is 4.4 m/s with a long reload - a missed shot is genuine distance for you.
avoid: Long open lanes and straight-line running.
Standing still to look at him while he is already aiming.

K20.threat: Punishment of the Damned reaches through walls, and Torment turns any down into a cage, which skips your anti-tunnel perks entirely.
counters: Do not walk in his trails. Torment is what makes the whole kit strong.
Cleanse Torment at a cage of atonement when you get a safe moment.
The ranged attack is slow to charge and travels a straight lane - step out of the lane or break line of sight.
He cannot use his power while carrying, and his M1 chase is ordinary, so normal loops still work.
avoid: Crossing his trails because it was the shorter path.
Standing in the same lane as a charged shot.

K21.threat: Chained rushes with a slam attack cover an entire tile in a second; his traversal rivals Hillbilly and his chase is far better.
counters: Play cluttered tiles. He needs surfaces to bounce off, but he also needs room to steer.
Hug the object tightly - a tight circle forces bumps that burn his rush tokens.
Never pre-run into open ground; a long open lane is a free lethal rush.
Count his rushes. Once the tokens are spent there is a real cooldown to exploit.
avoid: Wide-open pre-running between tiles.
Vaulting a window and running the straight line away from it.

K22.threat: Victor downs on his own and pins you in place while Charlotte walks over; against a slugging Twins the whole team snowballs down fast.
counters: Crush Victor whenever he is dormant near you - it removes the pressure and puts him on a long cooldown.
When Victor is charging a pounce, run at a wall or a tight corner so he splats.
Pick teammates up quickly; the entire power is built around leaving people on the ground.
Charlotte standing still to control Victor is free generator time - split the map and take it.
avoid: Leaving a downed teammate because Victor is nearby.
Running a long straight line while Victor is charged.

K23.threat: A sustained stream of blades filling a laceration meter - unlike Huntress there is no single projectile to dodge, just continuous fire.
counters: Break line of sight repeatedly. The meter decays, so denying him a full burst effectively resets the chase.
Use tall solid cover, not low walls - blades are small and slip through gaps.
Force reloads; he burns a lot of blades to finish one health state.
He is 4.4 m/s, so a real high-walled tile is a genuinely winning loop.
avoid: Running open lanes while he strafes behind you.
Holding a low-wall loop he can simply shoot over.

K24.threat: The tentacle out-ranges pallets and windows, and infection means the first hit on the whole team is effectively free once he is mutated.
counters: Take an early tentacle hit to get infected, then spend vaccines on the survivors who actually need them.
Kill zombies you walk past - they feed his mutation rate and clog your loops.
The tentacle telegraphs clearly; drop the pallet or vault before it lands rather than after.
Tight loops with high walls beat his range - low-wall tiles do not.
avoid: Hoarding vaccines for yourself.
Letting a zombie sit on the loop you plan to use.

K25.threat: Chain hunts interrupt everyone on the map at once, and the Lament Configuration forces someone to stop doing gens and solve it.
counters: Take the box early and solve it away from gens. Stalling only guarantees a chain hunt.
During a chain hunt, run through tight geometry - chains break on walls and corners.
Break a chain by putting an obstacle between it and you, then keep moving immediately.
Do not solve the box next to three teammates; he teleports straight to it.
avoid: Nobody picking up the box all match.
Solving the box on top of the generator the team still needs.

K26.threat: Crows hit through walls at any range and give her free information when repelled, so no loop is one-sided against her.
counters: Walk into the crows and swat them - repelling a crow before it fires is the entire counter.
Rotate off any tile she has already crow-sniped; the second visit is when it kills you.
Break line of sight so her long-range shots cannot confirm a target.
Crows telegraph with a sound and a short delay - move perpendicular to their line, not away from it.
avoid: Standing still to finish a gen while a crow is already charging at you.
Looping the same tile twice against an Artist.

K27.threat: Condemned stacks convert hook states into outright kills, and she can teleport to any powered TV, so no generator is ever far from her.
counters: Take tapes. Carrying a tape stops your Condemned building and turns that TV off.
Return the tape to a DIFFERENT TV than the one you took it from - that is what removes stacks.
She is invisible while demanifested, so line-of-sight warnings are worth more than terror-radius ones.
Do not repair standing in front of a powered TV while she is nearby.
avoid: Ignoring tapes because Condemned feels slow - it is what actually kills you.
Returning a tape to the same TV you pulled it from.

K28.threat: Locker-to-locker teleports plus Nightfall's total darkness give constant map pressure and a stealth approach you cannot see coming.
counters: Lock lockers you pass. A locked locker costs him time and gives you a stun window.
In Nightfall, stop running blind lines - walk, use sound, and stay on tiles you already know.
The Remnant is a return anchor: when you see one, expect him back at that exact spot.
Nightfall builds from injuries, so actually healing up slows his best phase down.
avoid: Hiding in a locker against The Dredge.
Leaving every locker on the map unlocked.

K29.threat: A double bound covers most tiles instantly, slams you into walls for an extra health state, and infects the whole team over time.
counters: Dodge sideways at the last moment - the bound is committed and a whiff is a long recovery.
Save sprays for high infection; the supply is limited and shared across the team.
Stay off walls when he is charging - a slam into geometry is the extra damage.
At loops, bait the bound over a pallet then loop back through the gap behind him.
avoid: Burning a spray at low infection because the meter looked scary.
Running along a wall in a straight line.

K30.threat: A summoned guard hunts you while he cuts you off, so most loops turn into a two-body pincer you cannot win.
counters: Grab the guard's standard - picking up the banner ends the hunt immediately.
Run away from the direction the guard is patrolling; never loop inside its path.
Leave the tile the moment a guard is summoned. Holding a pallet against two bodies loses every time.
The summon itself takes real time - that is your free distance to reach a fresh tile.
avoid: Looping a pallet while a guard is actively hunting you.
Walking past a banner you could have grabbed.

K31.threat: Drones zone entire tiles and a full Lock On injures you, leaves you Broken and tags you with a claw trap that broadcasts your position.
counters: Hack drones when you have the time; a disabled drone kills that tile's zoning for a while.
Do not linger in a scanned zone - take the one scan, keep moving, and leave.
Spread your gens out. Her power is area denial and she physically cannot cover the whole map.
A claw trap only comes off when its battery dies, so play the rest of that chase assuming she sees you.
avoid: Looping inside an active drone's scan zone.
Failing a hack mid-chase and feeding the Lock On meter.

K32.threat: Biopods watch tiles from range and Slipstream lets him teleport onto you from anywhere on the map.
counters: Print EMPs and actually use them - an EMP disables pods and strips Slipstream off you and nearby teammates.
Break the pod's line of sight; a pod only works on what it can currently see.
Fire EMPs for teammates near a hook, not just for yourself.
If a pod is tagging you, move out of its view before he presses the teleport, not after.
avoid: Never touching a printer for the entire match.
Finishing a gen while sitting in a pod's field of view.

K33.threat: Tunnel travel plus a long-range tail attack in Crawler Mode makes it fast, quiet and lethal at almost every tile.
counters: Carry turrets and place them - a turret staggers it and can knock it out of Crawler Mode entirely.
Cover the tile you intend to loop, not the gen you are leaving.
Turrets overheat and need repairing, so do not let one burn out firing at an empty corridor.
The tail attack has reach but a clear telegraph - a tight wall hug or a late vault beats it.
avoid: Leaving every turret sitting in its control station.
Standing in the open while it is in Crawler Mode.

K34.threat: Undetectable with map-wide fake footsteps, a dashing instant-hit, and a scamper that goes under dropped pallets.
counters: Ignore the footsteps. They are deliberate noise - trust line of sight and Killer Instinct instead.
A dropped pallet is not safety: he scampers under it, so keep moving rather than holding for a stun.
Slice and Dice is committed - a late hard turn at a wall makes him whiff and lose the dash.
He is very short, so he loses line of sight over cars and low walls too; use that to disappear mid-chase.
avoid: Standing behind a dropped pallet expecting it to hold.
Chasing the sound of footsteps to work out where he is.

K35.threat: A bouncing projectile makes you Weakened; after that any second blast area costs a health state, and his hallucinations are free teleport anchors.
counters: Stare him down to remove Weakened. It is a real mechanic and most survivors never use it.
Dispel hallucinations when you find them - each one left standing is a teleport he can take.
UVX bounces, so do not fight him in corners or hard against walls while he is charging.
While Weakened, break line of sight aggressively; the second blast is what actually downs you.
avoid: Running past hallucinations all match without dispelling any.
Backing into a corner while he charges UVX.

K36.threat: Four spells cover every gap a killer normally has - blocked pallets, wall-piercing projectiles, aura reveal and a fast flight.
counters: Open chests. Magic items are the designed counter to each spell and there is no other source for them.
Flight of the Damned passes through walls in a fixed spread - move perpendicular to the cast, never straight down its lane.
Mage Hand blocks a pallet for a few seconds; treat that pallet as gone and chain to the next tile.
Dispelling Sphere briefly disables your item, so reposition rather than trying to fight through it.
avoid: Ignoring every chest on the map.
Running directly away from a cast, which is exactly down its lane.

K37.threat: Three forms with no real weak one: Hellfire covers loops, Wolf tracks and pounces, and Bat is Undetectable fast traversal.
counters: Read the form first. Hellfire is a wide low wall of flame - move perpendicular or get behind real cover, not a low object.
In Wolf form, running leaves scent orbs he collects for Haste, so walk when you are not actively being chased.
Bat form cannot damage you; it is a travel form, so its arrival is a warning rather than a threat.
The Wolf pounce is committed - a tight turn at a corner makes it whiff and costs him his momentum.
avoid: Sprinting a straight line in front of a charged Hellfire.
Running everywhere while he is in Wolf form.

K38.threat: The dog grabs you and drags you back to her, and Houndsense turns your next injury into Deep Wound on top of it.
counters: A grab is not a guaranteed hit - stun the dog to break it, or have a teammate rescue you.
Endurance shortens the grab, so anti-tunnel perks carry real chase value in this matchup.
The Chase command is a mostly committed path with one redirect - break line of sight and turn hard.
Stay off the dog's Search Path; her speed bonus only builds while she follows it.
avoid: Running down the same open lane the dog was just sent along.
Leaving a grabbed teammate you were close enough to free.

K39.threat: Kagune leaps chain off vertical surfaces for very fast approaches, and a grab-attack applies Deep Wound plus a mark that keeps him Enraged.
counters: The Kagune has to attach to a vertical surface - open ground and low-object tiles deny his leaps outright.
Mend fully. A fully mended survivor loses the Kagune Mark, and once no marks remain his Enraged countdown starts running out.
He cannot grab-attack an already-marked survivor, so the marked player is the right one to take aggro for a moment.
Leaps end in a cooldown when he special-vaults a window or dropped pallet - forcing that vault is how you buy distance.
avoid: Looping tall walled tiles where every surface is a leap anchor.
Leaving Deep Wound half-mended - the mark is what keeps him Enraged.

K40.threat: A thrown Fire Axe embeds and applies Broken and Oblivious, and the security door network lets him travel the map while Undetectable.
counters: Remove an embedded axe as soon as you are safe - while it is in you, you are Broken and Oblivious.
Use camera view: it cycles every camera on the map, can reveal his aura to the whole team, and lets you travel to another door.
Watch the battery. Spamming cameras and doors drains it and locks the system out while he can still travel freely.
Never walk into a door he might be arriving at - moving into a door already in use is a grab.
avoid: Burning the whole battery on early sightseeing.
Reading a quiet map as a distant killer - door travel gives him Undetectable for 20 seconds after he exits.

K41.threat: Head form is faster, special-vaults and whips at range; a filled Leech meter injures you and leaves you Broken.
counters: Eat Glowing Fungus to drain the Leech meter, but not right before a hit - being hit ends the effect.
Head form cannot break dropped pallets and cannot gain Bloodlust, so dropping the pallet forces a form swap.
Read the terror radius: 32 m is Body form (pallet breaking, Regurgitate), 40 m is Head form (whip, Headlong Flight).
Intestinal Whip only damages you once you are Leeched, so keeping the meter low keeps his chase power non-lethal.
avoid: Letting the meter reach Leeched I - from there it fills the rest of the way on its own.
Holding a pallet in Head form and then eating the break anyway once he swaps.

K42.threat: Area attacks stack Worldbreaker tokens on you, and once Worldbreaker is active those same area attacks damage instead of tokening.
counters: Dodge the ground area, not the killer - both the Vine Attack and the Undergate return are area effects you can step out of.
Undergate returns give two tokens instead of one, so being caught by a re-entry is the fastest way to arm Worldbreaker.
Interact with the Grandfather Clocks - they speed the Worldbreaker timer down so the dangerous window ends sooner.
During Worldbreaker, treat every cast as a guaranteed injure and pre-drop tiles instead of holding them.
avoid: Standing on marked ground to squeeze out the last of a gen.
Ignoring the clocks and eating the full Worldbreaker duration.

K43.threat: Invisible and Undetectable while hunting, with a teleport-to-tile Jump Scare and thrown spikes that take a health state and pin you.
counters: While invisible he cannot see you or your scratch marks - standing still gives him a Mist Cloud, walking or running gives footprints, so change which one you are handing him.
Jump Scare drops him out of the invisible mode and reveals him with Haste, so once it happens the stealth phase is over and you know where he is.
Expect the pallet or window you are running to be the one he arrives at - pick tiles with two exits.
Do not let an injured teammate get spiked into a wall; that is an immobilise stacked on top of the down.
avoid: Repeating the same path - footprints show the route you took, not just where you are now.
Sitting still on a generator while he is invisible.

K44.threat: Divine Light passes through every obstacle, so cover does not protect you; getting hit applies Heresy, which sabotages repairs and enables Exile.
counters: Move perpendicular to the beam. It ignores walls, so crossing its path is the only real dodge.
The longer he charges and steers it, the faster and longer the cast - punishing an early cast is much easier than a fully charged one.
Heresy decays when you repent at a Shrine of Judgment, liberate an exiled teammate, or get saved from Exile yourself.
With Heresy on, Good repair skill checks cost you progress - hit Greats or take a non-repair job until it decays.
avoid: Hiding behind a wall from Divine Light.
Leaving an Exiled teammate to dodge the Seeds of Punishment alone.

survivorFundamentals: Generators are the only win condition. Time spent hiding is time the killer gets for free - if nobody is on a gen, nobody is winning.
Learn tiles, not killers. Knowing which loop is safe, which is a dead end and where the next pallet is beats any per-killer trick.
Pallet economy: pre-drop against instant-down and ranged powers, hold for the stun only against plain M1 killers who have to respect it.
Break line of sight before you break distance. Most killers track scratch marks, blood and sound, so the first thing to remove is information.
Take the chase you can win and leave the one you cannot. Rotating to a fresh tile is almost always better than dying at your favourite one.
Spread out. Two survivors on one gen is fine; three survivors in one corner of the map is a free four-hit snowball for the killer.
Unhook with a plan, not on instinct. A rescue into an open field next to a camping killer trades one hook state for two.
Heal where the killer is not. The safest heal is the one that happens on the other side of the map from the current chase.
killerFundamentals: Chase the closest, most-committed survivor. A chase you start because someone ran past you is usually a better chase than the one you walked to.
Drop a chase that is going badly. Thirty seconds at a strong tile against a good looper is worse than pressuring two gens.
Break the pallet or leave the tile - standing at a dropped pallet doing nothing is the single most common way killers lose time.
Pressure gens, not survivors. Damaging generators near the hook is what actually converts a down into map control.
Do not camp unless the endgame maths says to. A hook is bait, and standing next to it hands the other three survivors a free gen each.
Use your power for what it is good at. Most powers are either chase tools or map-pressure tools, and forcing the wrong one loses time.
Patrol on a route, not at random. Scratch marks, crows and gen sounds are free information most killers walk straight past.
Watch the gen spread. Three gens close together is worth defending; three gens on opposite ends of the map means you have already lost the map.
